note: Latin "habebat" (she had) is past where the Greek-English has "has"; the flight to the wilderness, the place prepared by God and the 1,260 days agree.

note: Both name the great dragon, ancient serpent, devil and Satan, deceiver of the whole world, thrown down to earth with his angels.

note: Both report worship of the dragon and the beast and the same two questions; the Latin "qui dedit" (who gave) is relative where Saints has because he gave.

note: Both give the beast a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies and authority to act for forty-two months.

note: Both say it was given to make war with the saints and conquer them, with authority over every tribe, people, tongue and nation.
